segments.english: Have you seen, to know the words of the Gaon Chavot Yair, how afraid and trembling he is to teach about separation, and relies on the words of the Gaon, the author of Shemen la-Ma'or, whose words were cited above, yet he is still afraid to say it outright, lest it slacken the hands from this holy wisdom, and how much he praises this wisdom, that one may merit it by learning it from a Kabbalist, and admits that anyone who holds himself back from studying it, after receiving it, is pushed away from its precinct; and also he permits engaging in the words of Kabbalah, and if he sees puzzling things before him, he may accept them in the faith of an artisan, and attribute it to his own shortness of understanding. If so, your two witnesses, the Ribash and Chavot Yair, will testify and bear witness against you that you invent things from your own heart; and where is his separation, which he explained, as you said? Did he not himself say, "Would that a spirit from on high were poured upon us," etc.? And I bring you proof that he merited the wisdom of Kabbalah, for in §272 he wrote, and these are his words: "that it is possible there are further matters of secret and hidden lore in two verses, alafim bat yakhil and gimel alafim bat, for at the sin of the first man three alafin were corrupted, of truth, of Adonai and of man, and there remained mat-din-dam against idolatry, illicit unions and bloodshed. And King David repaired truth; therefore he did not taste sleep at night, and did not manage to repair judgment, and also blood, as the Holy One, blessed be He, said: 'You shall not build the house, for you have shed much blood; only your son Solomon, for peace, etc.' And Solomon repaired two alafin, and with the alef of his father, three alafin were repaired, and the matter of Bat is known to li-yach, for the main flaw is there, and he further expanded on the secret of the matter there. And §276, on the matter of one who feeds a man blind in one of his eyes, and with all this I protested, for it seems to me that in both cases there is room to distinguish. However, where there is another fitting and suitable one like him, for it is known that the 248 limbs are a throne and a likeness of the 248 supernal lights, and the 248 limbs of the soul. And so, in every such case the throne is flawed, for according to the hidden there are heaps upon heaps of secret mysteries in the parts of the body, and there is a lack of flow in the cup of blessing." The one above, too, in the colophon of the book, wrote that he made 635 responses and gathered from them 232, the book Yehi Or, and it has the gematria of the four fillings of YHVH, 72, 63, 45, 52: the son who is in Abba and Imma, and Ze'ir and his Nukva. And further: let there be light. Yah, Yair. These are the sources of Tif'eret (Beauty) and Malkhut (Kingship) in Binah (Understanding), which is the light emanated on the first day. And he further expanded on many matters of secret and hidden lore. Also his father, the author of Shemen la-Ma'or, was a divine Kabbalist, for his verses were printed at the end of the book. And these are according to the Name of forty-two, and the twelve combinations of YHVH, and the twenty-four combinations of Adonai, and the Name of twenty-two. Also the true sage, the author of Menorat ha-Ma'or, was a divine Kabbalist, for in parashah 93 he wrote on "Baruch She'amar," that its way is in it, the number of the ten, the ten, etc. And in parashah 95 he wrote: "Kaddish is not said with fewer than ten," and the reason is that with ten the holiness is completed, which is above the ten sefirot. And in parashah 133 he wrote: "When Jacob was going down to Egypt, he saw that the exile had begun in him and in his seed, and he feared it and sacrificed sacrifices to the Fear of his father Isaac, so that the attribute of judgment would not be stretched out against him; and did this at Beersheba, which is a house of prayer for his fathers, and offered peace-offerings to complete to him all the attributes, as they expounded: 'shelamim, which cast peace', to complete to him the attribute of Gevurah (Might)." And in parashah 147 he wrote: "It is found that the completeness of holiness is in the ten, which allude to the ten havayot, and they are the ten sayings by which the world was created." And in parashah 153 he wrote: "And in the way of truth, that in six days the LORD made, etc. and on the seventh day it is Sabbath, and it has no mate, and the Assembly of Israel is its partner, as it is said: 'and the earth, and behold,' it is the Eighth Day of Assembly, for there everything is held back." And this is their saying: "The Eighth Day is a festival in itself," and the completion of the first is that it is the emanation of the earlier ones, and it is not in their unity. and whoever understands the havayot will be wise and find the truth. And in the colophon of the book he wrote: "And the fifth, I left out the grave matters, which are hidden and lofty, and there is no one who can attain them but a single individual in a generation." Thus he wished to write words of secret in his work, but because they are not fit for every person. Have you seen, to know that no one disputes the Kabbalah. neither the early ones nor the later ones, neither the many nor the individuals, neither the great nor the small. On the contrary, all agree that whoever merits the tradition from mouth to ear, there is no finer virtue for you than it. and that it is forbidden to expound and investigate it; but if he wishes, he should accept it in complete faith and not explain it by his human intellect. For he should attribute what troubles him to the shortness of his understanding, and not ruin any soul by thinking. And with this, all the words of the lowest of the low are complete. Order. And you shall return and hearken to the voice of the LORD.

grammar: The opening and the closing both begin 'Have you seen, to know' (הראית לדעת, 1 and 538): the speaker addresses the questioner with a rhetorical question.

The quotation from §272 is opened by כתב וז"ל (115-116) and runs to 267. The Holy One's words inside it (164-179) take single marks; the quoted words of Kabbalistic figures are in double marks where they stand.
The conditionals ואם כן (243) and א"כ (75) carry the argument: the respondent draws the consequence from the witnesses he has just named.
The fragment at 203-209 (וסי' קע"ו) has no verb in the Hebrew; the English supplies none and keeps it a reference.
שמיני רגל (488) is the Talmudic formula for the Eighth Day, which is Shemini Atzeret (481); the author argues from its separateness to the emanated day.
segments.note: The paragraph is the respondent's rebuke of the questioner, in the respondent's voice. The quotations from Chavot Yair are marked as far as the Hebrew shows them; the end of the §272 quotation is inferred (see apparatus). 'קראתי תיגר' (213) is read as the quoted author's own protest.
apparatus: Base text from Wikisource; the 1931 scan is not yet collated, so the base text is translated as it stands.
Quotation boundaries: the quotation from §272 is taken to run from שאפשר (117) to the cup of blessing (267); the Hebrew marks no closing formula, so the end is inferred from the sense.
1 Chr 22:8-9: the words 'לא תבנה הבית כי דמים רבים שפכת, רק בנך שלמה כי שלום' follow the author's wording, which differs from the verse.
Gen 1:3: יהי אור (296-297), an allusion without quotation marks.
Gen 31:42: פחד יצחק, 'Fear of Isaac' as a divine epithet (400-402).
Exod 20:11: ששת ימים עשה ה' (457-460), cut short with וכו' (461).
Deut 30:2: ואתה תשוב ושמעת בקול ה' (603-607), in the author's wording; the verse as usually printed reads differently.
Possible echo of Isa 32:15 in מי יתן ויערה עלינו רוח ממרום (98-103); not verified.
Numbers: 'Shemen la-Ma'or' and 'Menorat ha-Ma'or' are book titles, meanings in the token notes; Yehi Or is a title whose letters total 232.
context: Rabbi Isaac ben Sheshet (the Ribash) is a responsa author of the fourteenth century, cited here as an authority on Kabbalah's critics.
